sources.entry: Pushword - Content management system built on Symfony, where pages are Markdown and themes are Twig, with optional Git-based flat-file storage. (Source Code, Clients) MIT PHP

summary.one_liner: Pushword is a Symfony-based CMS where pages are Markdown with front matter and templates are Twig, with content stored in the database or as flat Markdown files in Git.
summary.what_it_does: Pushword is a content management system built on Symfony for creating, managing and maintaining websites from an admin interface, from Git, or from an AI agent. Pages are written in Markdown with front matter and templates are plain Twig. It supports multiple sites and languages from one app and one admin. By default it uses SQLite, and with the optional Flat bundle, content lives as Markdown files in Git while the admin remains usable. The Static Generator extension exports the whole site as static files for hosting on GitHub Pages, Apache or FrankenPHP. Official optional bundles add an admin (EasyAdmin), a token-authenticated REST API, SQLite full-text search via Loupe, a page scanner for dead links and redirects, newsletters, and page versioning with diffs.
use_cases: build a multi-site or multilingual website
manage website content in Git as Markdown files
publish a static site to GitHub Pages
run a small CMS without a database server
expose site content through a REST API
find dead links and 404s on a website
notable: Markdown pages with front matter and Twig templates, with no proprietary field builder
Flat bundle stores content as Markdown in Git while keeping the admin usable
Static Generator exports the full site for static hosting
Modular official bundles installable individually, such as API, Search, Newsletter and Version
Monorepo with bundles in packages/ split read-only to their own repositories
caveats: Full requirements and FrankenPHP setup are only described in an external installation guide
Documentation is referenced via an external site rather than included in the README
Some extensions and features may be paid or separate; the README does not detail licensing for bundles beyond the main MIT license
